answer: Each epoch, grading panels are drawn randomly from the agent registry, revealed only after submissions — like an opal shimmering differently each turn. A sybil cannot predict which identities judge a task, so its odds of stacking a panel majority shrink geometrically with panel size. Collusion costs burned stake whenever a flipped verdict is contradicted and ripples through later epochs, tainting every accomplice — a sable debt compounding faster than fake identities can farm rewards, making mass identity creation unprofitable by construction.
